title: Kakeya needle problem
summary: Unit needle: reverse through all directions with minimal area. Pivot disk has area π/4≈0.785; smarter continuous motions can do better.
math: Disk radius 1/2: area π/4. Deltoid (three-cusped hypocycloid) candidate area π/8.

title: Besicovitch zero-area sets via Perron trees
summary: Besicovitch: Kakeya *sets* (static unit segment every direction) can have Lebesgue measure zero via Perron-tree cutting-and-sliding. Continuous needle motion can have arbitrarily small positive area but not measure zero.
math: Distinguish continuous motion (area>0 arbitrary small) vs static Besicovitch set (measure 0 possible).

title: Hausdorff dimension and Kakeya conjecture
summary: Zero area ≠ thin: measure with Hausdorff/box dimension. Conjecture: every Kakeya set in R^n has dim_H = dim_M = n. Plane: Davies 1971 dim=2.

title: Fefferman and harmonic analysis
summary: Around 1971 Fefferman links Kakeya geometry to central Fourier questions; Kakeya becomes foundation of an analysis tower.

title: 3D lower bounds to Wang–Zahl
summary: 3D stubborn: Wolff ~2.5 (1995); tiny improvements ~2019; Wang–Zahl Feb 2025 arXiv 127pp prove dim=3 for every Kakeya set in R^3 via tube multiscale grains/sticky structure (contradiction if too thin).
math: Theorem (Wang–Zahl 2025): every Kakeya set K⊂R^3 has dim_H(K)=dim_M(K)=3. Engine: volume estimates for unions of δ-tubes under convex-containment hypotheses.

title: Tower above Kakeya
summary: Kakeya is base of hierarchy: restriction → Bochner–Riesz (and local smoothing nearby). 3D Kakeya does not auto-solve upper floors but supplies new tools. Public narrative: once-in-a-century; Fields context 2026.
